abstract:
<jats:p>
                    A randomized algorithm for a search problem is
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">pseudodeterministic</jats:italic>
                    if it produces a fixed canonical solution to the search problem with high probability. In their seminal work on the topic, Gat and Goldwasser [
                    <jats:xref ref-type="bibr">16</jats:xref>
                    ] posed as their main open problem whether prime numbers can be pseudodeterministically constructed in polynomial time.
                  </jats:p>
                  <jats:p>
                    We provide a positive solution to this question in the infinitely-often regime. In more detail, we give an
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">unconditional</jats:italic>
                    polynomial-time randomized algorithm
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">B</jats:italic>
                    such that, for infinitely many values of
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">n</jats:italic>
                    ,
                    <jats:inline-formula content-type="math/tex">
                      <jats:tex-math notation="LaTeX" version="MathJax">\(B(1^n)\)</jats:tex-math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    outputs a canonical
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">n</jats:italic>
                    -bit prime
                    <jats:inline-formula content-type="math/tex">
                      <jats:tex-math notation="LaTeX" version="MathJax">\(p_n\)</jats:tex-math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    with high probability. More generally, we prove that for every dense property
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">Q</jats:italic>
                    of strings that can be decided in polynomial time, there is an infinitely-often pseudodeterministic polynomial-time construction of strings satisfying
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">Q</jats:italic>
                    . This improves upon a subexponential-time construction of Oliveira and Santhanam [
                    <jats:xref ref-type="bibr">49</jats:xref>
                    ].
                  </jats:p>
                  <jats:p>
                    Our construction uses several new ideas, including a novel bootstrapping technique for pseudodeterministic constructions, and a quantitative optimization of the uniform hardness-randomness framework of Chen and Tell [
                    <jats:xref ref-type="bibr">11</jats:xref>
                    ], using a variant of the Shaltiel–Umans generator [
                    <jats:xref ref-type="bibr">51</jats:xref>
                    ].
                  </jats:p>
title: Polynomial-Time Pseudodeterministic Construction of Primes
